| S1-F2 | DONE | 2026-10-12 | Outbox hardening (ADR 0014 implemented). **Poll only:** `emit()` and `replayOutboxBatch` send no NOTIFY; dispatcher lanes poll every 250 ms and claim again at once after any non-empty batch; `DATABASE_URL_LISTEN`, `@inmolink/db` `listen()` and the `app_listen` follow-up are gone (config, worker, `.env*.example`, Kamal, Ansible). **Per-tenant fair claim:** one SQL statement enumerates the agencies with due rows (recursive loose index scan, one probe each, ≤ `maxAgenciesPerClaim` = 64 agencies per claim, per-lane rotating cursor with wrap-around so every agency is reached within ⌈due agencies / 64⌉ claims), shares the batch by water-filling (small agencies take all they have, the rest split the remainder), takes each agency's oldest rows with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` and interleaves them round-robin; the per-agency count probes stop at the equal share and then at the level the small agencies leave the others, so a claim reads about 2 × `batchSize` index entries for counting plus the rows it locks — O(batchSize + 64), not O(backlog) or O(agencies). Migration 0029 re-keys `outbox_events_pending_idx` to `(agency_id, available_at, id) where processed_at is null`; 0030 (custom) sets aggressive autovacuum/analyze thresholds on `outbox_events` (queue table: insert, two updates, delete). **One `PLATFORM_AGENCY_ID`:** new leaf `@inmolink/platform/tenancy`, re-exported by `platform/outbox`; `db/tenancy/rls.ts` and the registry predicates import it; a workspace test fails if the literal appears anywhere else. **Subscriber idempotency** is a PATTERNS §8 / workers.md rule (delivery tracked per event; a retry re-runs every subscriber) instead of per-subscriber tracking. Tests: `[S1-F2]` 50,000-event burst + 9 other agencies → every other agency's event is in the first batch of 500 (dispatcher with a 5,000-agency cap, so the dozens of agencies earlier suites leave in the shared table do not push ours out of the first rotation); 150 agencies × 3 rows with 64 per claim → three claims in rotation, each agency served by exactly one claim, no agency twice before all once; idle lane picks up an event in < 500 ms (250 ms poll + delivery); platform id defined once. **Perf (local, Windows + Docker Desktop):** outbox dispatch of 30 k events (30 agencies × 1,000), final build: per-10 k windows 1,522 / 2,850 / 3,666 ev/s, overall 2,342, measured right after a 170 k-row insert/delete churn on the table; the one-pass build an hour earlier on a quiet table: 3,798 / 3,370 / 3,885, overall 3,670 (S0-06 baseline: 1,806 / 3,075 / 3,085, overall 2,494); zero loss across a redis-queue restart. Claim plan (`EXPLAIN ANALYZE`, all index scans, no Seq Scan): 50 k burst + 9 × 1 + 107 platform rows → 13 ms; 600 agencies × 200 rows → 74–124 ms, of which locking the 500 rows is ~65 ms on this disk (the pre-S1-F2 claim on the same data: 177–252 ms; the fair-share CTEs alone, no locks: 5–6 ms) |

Tests: `[S1-F3]` flag read inside an aborted request transaction succeeds with the reader and fails (`25P02`) without it; `withTenant` with one query = 1 statement / 3 round trips with the settings visible; `withSystem` escapes a reason containing quotes and semicolons; `withGlobalRead` is read-only `app_user` with no tenant; backoff unit test |

## Decisions
<!-- Assumptions Claude made where the plan was silent, and proposed ADRs awaiting approval. -->
- 2026-10-14 · **Commission and split stay in basis points in the API (S1-06-F1), percentages in the form only.** The backlog line said the settings API exposes percentages; the existing `Commission` contract (`basisPoints`) and the listing DTO in PATTERNS use basis points, so the API keeps one unit (integers, no float rounding) and the dashboard converts. Needs Shahzaib's confirmation (S1 review).
- 2026-10-14 · **Every agency has a default commission (S1-06-F1).** "Not set" is gone: agencies that had none were backfilled to 5 % / 50 % by migration 0033. Needs Shahzaib's confirmation (S1 review).
- 2026-10-14 · **Agency admins see the staff member's reason, not who (S1-F9).** Transparency for the agency (PLAN §12): the access record shows when staff acted, as which member and the stated reason; staff identities stay with Inmolink, as in the agency audit log. The start form tells staff the reason is shown to admins.
- 2026-10-14 · **Super admins see and end any staff session (S1-F9).** RLS on `staff_impersonations` for `app_staff` widened to own rows or an active SUPER_ADMIN (their own `staff_users` row); inserts stay own-only and guard 0028 still limits updates to ending once.
- 2026-10-14 · **Narrowed tenant read: registry `userSelect` + column grants (S1-F10, ADR 0016).** Column grants over a `SECURITY DEFINER` reader: no new definer function, and the database itself refuses `select *`, filters and ordering on the hidden column. A column added later is unreadable to `app_user` until `pnpm db:rls` runs (the guard says so). Supersedes the S1-F9 proposal.
- 2026-10-14 · **2FA enrolment step-up is the fresh password, not an emailed link (S1-F8).** It stops someone using an open session; it does not stop someone who has the password and enrols first. The "2FA turned on" email to the owner covers that case. An emailed enrolment link can be added later if needed.
- 2026-10-14 · **2FA lockout vs guessing (S1-F8).** Code checks are limited per user+client, so one client cannot lock the owner out. A user-wide ceiling of 200 a day stays as a backstop against guessing spread over many networks (≈ 0.06 % per day against 3 valid codes). Reaching it takes at least 10 networks, and only then does the owner have to wait.
- 2026-10-10 · **Pricing is configurable.** €800/yr and every other price, cap and reward in PLAN are working figures, not fixed values. Plans, prices, limits and add-ons are data (catalog synced to Stripe, staff-editable); never constants in code. PLAN §0 and §11 annotated. (Shahzaib)
- 2026-10-10 · **Node.js 24 LTS** for dev and CI; production servers support 22 and 24, so root `engines.node` is `>=22 <25`. Record in ADR 0001. PLAN §5.8 updated. (Shahzaib)
- 2026-10-10 · **PostgreSQL 17+** (PLAN §5.1 said 16; §5.8, S0-02 and PATTERNS §13 `MERGE … RETURNING merge_action()` need 17). §5.1 corrected.
- 2026-10-10 · **Next.js latest stable** (PLAN §5.2 said 15; §5.8 says latest stable). §5.2 corrected; exact version pinned in ADR 0001.
- 2026-10-10 · **Email and storage adapters** have no S0 task. Build `platform/email` (Resend/SES drivers, Mailpit locally) inside S0-09, and `platform/storage` (R2/MinIO, private buckets, signed URLs) inside S1-03, both following the platform adapter pattern. (Shahzaib approved)
- 2026-10-10 · **Forward dependencies:** S3-10 depends on S4-02, and S5-06 depends on S11-04. S3 and S5 can close with those two tasks marked `BLOCKED S4-02` / `BLOCKED S11-04`; each task finishes when its dependency is DONE.
- 2026-10-10 · Repo path is `E:\Repos\InmolinkCRM` (docs said `E:\Repos\Inmolink`; PLAN §22 and BUILD-GUIDE fixed). Remote: `https://github.com/gr8xpert/Inmolink-CRM.git`.
- 2026-10-10 · **TypeScript 6.0.3, not 7.0** (S0-01). TS 7 has no JS compiler API yet, and Next API-mode type checking, dependency-cruiser, SDK codegen and tsdown d.ts depend on it. Revisit at each sprint review (ADR 0001).
- 2026-10-10 · **pnpm 10.33.2 pinned, pnpm 12 deferred** (S0-01). pnpm 10's auto-switch to `pnpm@12.10.1` fails on this machine because the user path contains a space (`Shah PC`). Upgrade after installing pnpm 12 globally (ADR 0001).
- 2026-10-10 · **Package exports use a `@inmolink/source` condition** (S0-01). Typecheck, Vitest and tsx resolve TypeScript source; builds and Next resolve tsdown `dist/`. App packages are named `@inmolink/app-<name>`. `apps/wp-plugin` stays outside the pnpm workspace (PHP tooling).
- 2026-10-10 · **Stubbed root scripts exit 1** with the owning task ID, so nothing silently pretends to work. `verify` gains `check:boundaries` (S0-12) and `test:isolation` (S0-05) when those tasks land.
- 2026-10-10 · **PostgreSQL 18** (S0-02). PG 18.6 is the newest major with PostGIS 3.6, pgvector 0.8.7 and pg_partman 5.5 all packaged (PGDG), within "17+". Image `inmolink/postgres:18-3.6` is built from `postgis/postgis:18-3.6`. Production must run the same major (S0-15).
- 2026-10-10 · **MinIO image from `pgsty/minio`** (S0-02). Upstream MinIO stopped publishing Docker images; `pgsty/minio` and `pgsty/mc` are the community builds of the same server and client. Local/CI only — production storage is R2. If that fork stalls, swap to any S3-compatible server; the storage adapter (S1-03) only speaks S3.
- 2026-10-10 · **`pnpm verify` needs Docker** (S0-02). Root `test:int:root` (tests/infra) runs in `verify` and its global setup runs `docker compose --profile test up -d --wait`. Package integration tests from S0-04 on use the same test stack. The stack stays up between runs; `pnpm infra:down` stops both profiles.
- 2026-10-10 · **Bootstrap superuser `postgres` is for ops only** (S0-02). `DATABASE_URL_ADMIN(_POOLED)` serve health checks and scripts. App roles (`app_owner`, `app_user`, `app_system`, `app_public`) are created in S0-04. PgBouncer finds them through `auth_query`, so S0-04 does not need to edit `userlist.txt`.
- 2026-10-10 · **pg and ioredis were added in S0-02**, earlier than planned, for the health script. Versions match ADR 0001: pg 8.23.1 and ioredis 6.0.0. ioredis 6 defaults to RESP3, and the health script passes `protocol: 2`. S0-06 must choose the protocol on purpose for BullMQ.
- 2026-10-10 · **Outbox is a STRICT, append-only tenant table** (S0-06). Request transactions insert their own agency's events (RLS `for insert`, INSERT-only grant); platform-wide events use the nil UUID and only `withSystem()` can write them. The dispatcher and replay read/ack via `withSystem()`. The registry gained `appendOnly` (PATTERNS §2).
- 2026-10-10 · **`@inmolink/platform` does not depend on `@inmolink/db`** (S0-06): `emit` takes a structural `SqlExecutor`; the dispatcher gets `runSystem` (= `withSystem`) and `listen` injected. The table schema lives in `packages/db/src/schema/outbox.ts`, the SQL in platform/outbox (column names kept in sync, covered by the int tests). Outbox/queue integration tests live at the root (`tests/queue`, `tests/perf`) because the root depends on both.
- 2026-10-10 · **LISTEN needs a direct connection** (S0-06): PgBouncer transaction mode cannot hold LISTEN, so `DATABASE_URL_LISTEN` (optional, workers only, refused for APP_ROLE=http in production; `listen()` also calls `assertSystemAllowed()`) points straight at Postgres. It uses the `app_system` credential today; a dedicated no-grant `app_listen` login role is a follow-up for S0-15 (security audit). Without it the dispatcher polls (1 s).
- 2026-10-10 · **Fair share on open-source BullMQ** (S0-06): BullMQ groups are Pro-only, so `platform/queue/fairness.ts` sets priority = the group's backlog depth (interleaves groups) and enforces `concurrencyPerGroup` with a Lua lease set (a job that finds its group full goes back to delayed). Jobs without `group` keep priority 0 and run before grouped ones — give every tenant-scoped job a group. The batched script spans many keys, so redis-queue must stay a single node (or share a hash-tag prefix).
- 2026-10-10 · **ioredis protocol 2 for BullMQ** (S0-06, resolves the S0-02 note): RESP2 pinned on every queue connection. Producer: `maxRetriesPerRequest: 1` + auto-pipelining (an enqueue fails fast, so the dispatcher retries the event instead of stalling); workers: `maxRetriesPerRequest: null` (BullMQ requirement).
- 2026-10-10 · **Throughput check is the best 10 k window** (S0-06). On this Windows + Docker Desktop machine with ~60 % background CPU, single windows vary 1.5–4.7 k ev/s (autovacuum, AOF rewrite, desktop load); overall rates were 2.35–2.9 k in the last runs. The test reports all windows + overall and asserts the best window ≥ 2,000. CI on Linux (S0-14) should assert the overall rate instead. `test:perf:root` runs last in `verify` (turbo `dependsOn`) and restarts the **test** redis-queue with plain `docker restart` (`docker compose restart` drops the published port on Docker Desktop for Windows).
- 2026-10-10 · **Follow-ups from S0-06 reviews (accepted for now):** (1) the outbox claim is global FIFO — one agency's 100 k-event import delays other agencies' events; add a per-agency cap per claim before R2 imports (jobs downstream already have fair share). (2) `emit` sends NOTIFY, which serializes commits of notifying transactions on a global lock; measure with many concurrent emitters before R2 imports and drop NOTIFY for polling if it shows. (3) every dispatcher poll writes a `withSystem` audit log line; give routine system queries a quieter audit level in S0-10. (4) `last_error` and DLQ entries keep raw error text — tenants cannot read either (outbox is INSERT-only for app_user; the DLQ is Redis, ops only). (5) no DLQ re-enqueue tool yet; add it with the ops runbook (S0-15).
- 2026-10-10 · **Feature flag overrides live on the global `feature_flags` row** (S0-07) as `enabled_for`/`disabled_for` agency ID arrays, not a STRICT per-agency table: a STRICT table would let `app_user` switch its own agency's flags on. Consequences, accepted: any `app_user` session can read which agency IDs are on a pilot (no endpoint exposes rows; `flag()` returns a boolean for `ctx.tenant` only — never return raw rows to tenants, keep descriptions free of customer names); flags are **dashboard/worker only** (`app_public` has no grant; feed-api would need a deliberate `publicRead` or a read model). - 2026-10-10 · **Rate-limit counters share redis-cache** (S0-07, allkeys-lru): eviction under memory pressure can reset a counter, and non-credential rules fail open when Redis is down (PLAN §5.4 degrade). Credential rules (`auth.*`, `password.*`, `2fa.*`) are forced to fail closed. If cache pressure is ever seen evicting auth counters, move them to a small `volatile-lru` Redis DB (S0-15). Windows use the app server clock (NTP-synced), not Redis `TIME` — skew only loosens a limit slightly.
- 2026-10-10 · **Cache single-flight is per process** (S0-07): N app processes can run the loader N times on a cold key; no distributed lock (accepted — bounded by node count). Other processes' in-process (`local`) copies and flag snapshots expire within 60 s of an invalidation.

Reason: security audit — an untenanted key plus single-flight would serve one agency's RLS-scoped result to another.
- 2026-10-10 · **Windows test-run instability, open** (S0-07): (1) vitest fork workers intermittently die with exit 0xC0000409 (native abort, no stderr) in int/perf files — ~2 in 20 runs on this machine, seen in pre-existing S0-06 files as well as new ones; a re-run passes. Not reproduced on HEAD in 8 runs, which is not conclusive. Mitigations: `adapters` files run serially and after `infra`+`queue`. Re-check on Linux CI (S0-14); if it persists, try `pool: 'threads'` for the int projects. (2) the S0-06 perf test's `docker restart` of redis-queue-test can come back **without its published port** on Docker Desktop, after which every queue test fails to reach Redis; `restartRedisQueue()` now checks `docker port` and recreates the container (same AOF volume) when the port is missing. Prior test runs also leave large AOF files in redis-queue-test (5.5 s load); `pnpm infra:down` + volume prune resets it.

Apps reach the database only through `@inmolink/core` (`configureDb`, `closeDb`, `pingDb`, `withRequestCtx`, `createOutboxDispatcher`, re-exported in `core/src/runtime.ts`). Exception: app **tests** may import `@inmolink/db/testing` (devDependency) to bring the test stack up. S0-12's dependency-cruiser rules must encode exactly this.

- 2026-10-10 · **Graceful shutdown order** (S0-08): `draining` (readiness 503) → optional `SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_DELAY_MS` (default 0; kamal-proxy drains on its own) → `closing` (new requests 503 with `Connection: close`) → `app.close()` waits for in-flight requests → queues/cache/db close. On Windows, SIGTERM cannot be delivered to a child process, so the boot test asserts exit 0 only on Linux; the drain itself is tested in-process.

No per-request DB check in the API; revocation = no new tokens after a password reset (`session_version`), so a stolen token lives ≤ 15 min. Display names reject links (no `://`, dots must be followed by a space) because they appear in our emails.

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-02 users, roles, invites, seats.**
  - **No `session_version` bump on role change or deactivation** (deviates from the S1-01 note). `users` is reachable only by app_auth, so a tenant session cannot bump it. Deactivation is a membership state (`agency_members.deactivated_at`) checked at login (same error as a wrong password), by `isSessionValid` (the web session ends at its next Auth.js re-check, ≤ 5 min), by `issueAccessToken` (no new tokens) and per request by `withMemberCtx` (the API refuses the user on the next call, even with an unexpired token). A role change needs no revocation: the role is read per request.
  - Roles by family: AGENCY_ADMIN manages AGENCY_ADMIN/AGENT, DEVELOPER_ADMIN the developer roles (policy + guard trigger 0009). "Only AGENCY_ADMIN" in the task covers DEVELOPER_ADMIN for developer tenants, as in the agencies policy.

  - An email that already has an account cannot accept (`INVITE_EMAIL_IN_USE`, one agency per user). Known gap (review): an unconfirmed sign-up squatting the email blocks invites; follow-up — let a valid invite take over an unconfirmed, untouched sign-up (S1-F4).
  - `agency_members.name/email` copy `users` at join time; a future profile/email change must update the copy through an event.

Unverified agencies are capped at 5 seats (security review M2), plus invite rate limits per tenant (100/h) and per user (50/day).
  - No `Idempotency-Key` on `POST /v1/invites` (no middleware exists yet): re-inviting an email replaces its open invite, so retries do not duplicate. Add with the idempotency platform work.

The use case takes a `CtxRunner` (check → store outside any transaction → record; the object is deleted if recording fails). PATTERNS §4 documents the shape.

  - Staff log in with a password until S1-04; no production staff grants before then (ADR 0015). Superseded by S1-04: staff must pass 2FA.

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-04 two-factor authentication.**
  - **Required roles:** staff, `AGENCY_ADMIN` and `DEVELOPER_ADMIN` (PLAN §12 says "agency admins"; the developer admin has the same powers over its account). Anyone who opts in is held to it too.
  - **Enforced at the access-token mint**, not per page: every dashboard read or write needs a token, so a session that owes 2FA reaches nothing. The 2FA and security pages call identity directly (auth-flow exception, ADR 0004).
  - **Session upgrade by proof:** Auth.js hands browser-supplied data to the `jwt` callback on `update`, so the session trusts only an identity HMAC proof (2 minutes, bound to user and session version). It is not bound to one JWT, so it could be replayed into another session of the same user within 2 minutes, but it never reaches the browser.
  - **Remembered browsers** are a stateless signed cookie (no table): a password reset or re-enrolment ends all of them; no per-browser revoke yet (S1-F8).
  - The enrolment page creates the pending secret on GET (idempotent: reused until confirmed). Moving it behind a POST is in S1-F8.
  - The TOTP window stays ±1 step (clock drift); the daily per-user cap (20) bounds slow guessing to about 0.3 % a day per account (security review).
  - New dependency: qrcode 1.5.4 (+ @types/qrcode, dev) in web, for the enrolment QR code, rendered server-side as an inert `<img>` data URL.

- 2026-10-11 · **S1-F4 identity follow-ups.**
  - **Throttle, not debounce:** the queue's `debounceMs` is trailing (the email would leave 10 minutes after the *last* login); the rate limiter gives a leading edge — the first unverified login sends at once. The sliding window means the next resend comes 10–20 minutes later.
  - **Recurring jobs** are the platform's first scheduler (S1-08's partition maintenance will use it). A renamed or removed recurring job leaves its scheduler in Redis: remove it with `removeJobScheduler` in the same change.
  - `identity.getMe` takes no `ctx` (exception to rule 4): it reads only verified token claims.
  - Request ids trust the configured edge header like the API; this assumes the web origin is reachable only through the edge (kamal-proxy behind Cloudflare). Locking the origin to edge traffic is an S1-F5/infra concern.
  - Code review flagged invite tokens (7-day TTL) as kept too long — they live in `agency_invites`, not `auth_tokens`; the prune now also goes by `used_at`, so "used more than 7 days ago" holds for any TTL.

Another Cloudflare customer pointing a proxied zone at our IP is still possible — revisit with Cloudflare for SaaS (S12) or an mTLS-capable proxy.

- 2026-10-12 · **S1-05 API keys.**
  - **`api_keys` is PUBLIC_READ** (usable keys only): feed-api runs as `app_public` and must find a key before the tenant is known. `app_public` sees HMAC hashes of 256-bit secrets plus metadata (name, creator, last use). **Proposed:** column-level SELECT for `app_public` (only the columns `findUsableApiKeyByPrefix` reads) — the RLS generator cannot express column grants yet.
  - **HMAC, not Argon2id**, for key hashes: every website request checks a key; 256-bit secrets cannot be brute-forced offline. `live` keys only when `DEPLOY_ENV`/`NODE_ENV` is production; other-environment keys are refused.
  - **Revocation ≤ 60 s:** Redis 25 s + in-process 15 s; revoke/rotate deletes the shared entry, other processes' copies expire within 15 s. Misses are never cached.
  - **Rate tiers:** agencies get STANDARD (600/min per key) plus a per-agency ceiling (3,000/min); HIGH is not settable through the agency API until plans exist (S13).
  - **Publishable keys** carry only read scopes + `search:ai`. For S7: write scopes on publishable keys need Turnstile; CORS must echo only an allowlisted `Origin` with `Vary: Origin`, never `*`, never for secret keys.
  - `authenticateApiKey` takes no `ctx` (runs before the tenant is known, like `getMe`). Key code sits in `api-keys.ts`/`api-keys-repo.ts` (identity `repo.ts` was ~680 lines).
  - Deferred: editing a key's name/scopes/origins (create a new key), `Idempotency-Key` on create, CORS and real v2 routes (S7), audit-log rows (S1-08 — events already carry actor and impersonator), `/perf-check` (no hot feed-api endpoint yet; lookup is one unique-index probe behind the cache).

  - **Gap → S1-F9:** a disabled staff account or bumped session version is not re-checked per request (`app_staff` cannot read `users`); bounded by the 15-min token, the mint re-checks both. Members can read session `reason` through RLS (no endpoint shows it).
  - Audit vocabulary grew: `agencies.profile.updated`, `staff.tenant.read`, `staff.members.read`, `staff.impersonation.started|ended`.
  - Keyset lists sort on millisecond-truncated time (one sort of the filtered rows instead of index order); fine for current list sizes — PATTERNS §5 has the alternative (`timestamp(3)` columns) for large lists. Indexes on partitioned tables at scale: `ON ONLY` parent + `CONCURRENTLY` per partition + ATTACH (PATTERNS §5).
  - New follow-up **S1-F9** (BACKLOG) for the remaining review items.

- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F3 platform and core cleanups.**
  - The BEGIN round trip carries the settings by intercepting the pooled client's first `query` call for the transaction (Drizzle offers no hook before `begin`; `SET LOCAL` needs literals just the same). Values are escaped with node-pg's `escapeLiteral`; the UUID values are regex-checked before, the reasons come from code. A multi-statement simple query cannot carry bind parameters, which is why literals are used at all. Drizzle sees the combined statement as `begin`, so `countQueries` excludes it as transaction control.
  - `countQueries` is a Drizzle logger hook, not a pg wrapper: `withSystemClient` (COPY streams) is not counted, and overlapping counts see each other's statements — count one scenario at a time. Budgets are written in statements (begin/commit excluded) unless a test asks for round trips.
  - The flag reload reads as `app_user` through `withGlobalRead` (read-only, no tenant), not `app_system`: the dashboard and workers have that URL, and `feature_flags` is a global table `app_user` may read. Without a reader (unit tests, scripts) the reload falls back to the caller's transaction as before.
  - Over-cap retry backoff is per process (an in-memory map by job id, cleared when the job runs, dead-letters or releases its slot); a job that moves to another worker starts again at the first delay — bounded, and no Redis round trip per retry.
  - Review and audit outcomes (S1-F3): the BEGIN hook is an own property deleted after the transaction (a stored `.bind()` grew per transaction); the transaction fails before any statement if BEGIN was not intercepted (audit settings must never be silently absent); the pooled client is destroyed only when a control statement (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) failed, never for an error thrown by `fn`; `withSystem`/`withStaff` refuse NUL in reasons; pools pin `client_encoding: 'UTF8'` (the only encoding under which `escapeLiteral` is byte-safe); flag reads serve an expired snapshot while the reload runs or fails (stale-while-revalidate), so a saturated `app_user` pool cannot stall requests at the 60-second expiry; the generated policy test asserts every `CLIENT_MODE_ALLOWED` entry is a read action.
- 2026-10-12 · **S1-F2 outbox hardening.**
  - A lane claims again without a pause after *any* non-empty batch, not only a full one (ADR 0014 says "while batches are full"): a fair batch is cut by rounding and a trickle of small agencies can leave it under-full while rows are still due. An idle lane still costs one index probe per 250 ms.
  - The fair claim serves at most `maxAgenciesPerClaim` = 64 agencies per claim (each costs an enumeration probe, a count probe and a locking scan: 600 agencies with backlog measured 157 ms per claim uncapped, far over the 20 ms SQL budget) and rotates a per-lane cursor across claims, so every due agency is reached within ⌈agencies / 64⌉ claims — with 5,000 agencies all importing at once, under 80 claims, i.e. a few seconds, instead of one batch. Lanes keep independent cursors; `SKIP LOCKED` keeps them off each other's rows.
  - `outbox_events_pending_idx` now leads with `agency_id`. There is no longer an index ordered by `available_at` alone: nothing reads the oldest pending row globally (replay is by `id`; a future "oldest pending event age" metric would group by agency or add its own index).
  - Autovacuum settings for `outbox_events` are a custom migration (0030: vacuum at 1 % / 5,000 dead rows, insert-vacuum at 5 % / 10,000, analyze at 2 % / 5,000, cost delay 1 ms). No `fillfactor`: the claim and the acknowledgement both change indexed columns, so updates are not HOT anyway.
  - Delivery stays tracked per event (one `processed_at`), and PATTERNS §8 / workers.md now require each subscriber to be idempotent on its own, instead of a per-subscriber delivery table. Subscribers already enqueue jobs with stable IDs; the extra table would add a write per subscriber per event on the hottest path for a guarantee consumers must not rely on anyway (at-least-once).
  - Code review (S1-F2): the first cut counted due rows per agency up to `batchSize` — O(agencies × min(backlog, 500)), measured 221–339 ms (1.5 s cold) for 600 agencies × 200 rows. The probe now stops at the equal share `ceil(batchSize / agencies)`; agencies at the share are recounted up to the level the small ones leave them (a one-pass cap under-filled a 50 k burst + 107 platform rows + 46 small agencies to 356 of 500); the water level comes from the first agency at or above its probe limit. A big agency with fewer rows than a level raised twice can still leave slots empty in that batch; the lane claims again at once.
  - Security audit (S1-F2): the pg_hba rules and the ufw rule that let app hosts and the `kamal` network reach Postgres 5432 directly as `app_system` existed only for LISTEN; both are removed, so a compromised app host can reach the database only through PgBouncer (`127.0.0.1`). Migration 0029 rebuilds the pending index non-concurrently (fine before launch; a live system would need a `CONCURRENTLY` out-of-transaction migration).
  - `pnpm verify` (9 min, 58 tasks) had one failure on this machine: `tests/isolation/guard.int.test.ts` lost its `applyRls` lock-timeout race (`set local lock_timeout = '5s'`, "canceling statement due to lock timeout") while the queue and perf suites were hammering `outbox_events` in parallel. `pnpm test:isolation` alone passes (342 tests). Watch for a repeat; if it recurs, make `test:isolation` depend on `test:int:root` / `test:perf:root` in turbo.json so the ALTER TABLE statements never compete with the outbox load.
  - Two `pnpm verify` runs on this machine ended on unrelated Windows flakes: a Vitest fork worker of `@inmolink/app-api` `test:int` died with 0xC0000409 (the crash the vitest config already works around for the root projects with `pool: 'threads'`) and, once, the isolation guard's `applyRls` lock timeout above. Each suite passes when re-run alone. Tried `pool: 'threads'` in the shared Vitest preset: the core int suite's main process then died with 0xC0000409 twice under `verify` (a native-module crash in a worker thread takes the whole run down; forks are isolated), so forks stay and `pnpm verify` caps Turbo at `--concurrency=4` instead; `test:isolation` now depends on every package's int suite so `applyRls` never competes with them.
  - The throughput perf test keeps its `[S0-06]` tag and its ≥ 2,000 events/s check (ADR 0014 keeps it); the `restartRedisQueue` helper's `docker compose up --force-recreate` can fail on Docker Desktop for Windows (the container stays `Created`): start `redis-queue-test` by hand and re-run.
- 2026-10-12 · **S1-10 dashboard shell.**
  - Capabilities live in a core module of their own (`modules/dashboard`), not in identity: the aggregator imports every module's `index.ts`, so putting it in identity would have made the lowest module depend on the ones above it. Modules that add a dashboard section register it there (PATTERNS: a module without tables is fine; it has no repo or schema).
  - `identity.members.read` is now refused in Client Mode (S1-02 policy change): the member roster (names, emails, roles) is internal data, like the partner list (`agencies.preferred.read`). Client Mode is still hard-wired off (`core/member.ts`), so nothing changes for users yet; the dashboard hides the Team section once it is live.
  - The web mints one api token per render and audience and asks `/v1/staff/me` once per render (React `cache` keyed by primitives): the shell, the layout and the page share them. Before, a staff console page minted three times and called the staff API twice.
  - `lighthouse` 13.5.0 is a root devDependency, used only by `tests/e2e/shell.spec.ts` (the accessibility acceptance check; the same tool measures the public pages' Lighthouse ≥ 90 later). It drives a second Playwright Chromium (`channel: 'chromium'`, DevTools on `PORTS.devtools`) and sends the session cookie as an extra header — fine while the dashboard loads only same-origin assets; switch to CDP `Network.setCookie` if a third-party script is ever embedded.
  - `pnpm perf:bundle` reads `.next/build-manifest.json` and the per-route `page_client-reference-manifest.js` files without evaluating them (Next 16 Turbopack prints no first-load sizes). CI runs it with `--if-present` because PR runs build only affected apps.
  - The e2e TOTP helper now tries the current step first, then the next, then the previous (it used to start with the previous step and lost a code computed just before a 30-second boundary: one password-reset run failed that way).

- 2026-10-14 · **S1-F6 database and Redis operations.**
  - **Rate limits on redis-queue, not a third Redis:** the task offered redis-queue with a prefix or a `volatile-lru` split; `volatile-lru` would still evict counters (they carry TTLs), so redis-queue it is. Production connects as an ACL user confined to `inl:rl:*`; the test runs the real limiter as that user.
  - **Residual risks (security review), accepted for now:** (1) redis-queue has no `maxmemory`: a flood of distinct identities creates counter keys (each lives ≤ 2 windows) in the Redis that also holds jobs — add memory and `inl:rl:*` key-count alerts with the monitoring dashboards; a `maxmemory` cap would fail BullMQ writes too. (2) All apps share the `inl:rl:*` prefix, so a compromised feed-api could reset web's login counters; per-app prefixes and users if that matters. (3) api still holds the full `REDIS_QUEUE_URL` (it enqueues); a producer ACL user is a later hardening. (4) The limiter now shares a single-threaded Redis with BullMQ: a latency spike over 200 ms fails closed on `auth.*` rules — watch the limiter's fail-closed warnings.
  - **max_db_connections is per database, shared by every role:** long app_system work can still starve request roles, which now get a fast error instead of a 120 s hang. Per-role pool sizes when Stage B splits workers out.
  - **Users-phase budget:** the perf test asserts 15.2 s / 5 = 3.04 s, the review's figure; on this machine the old code took 6.1 s, so the same-machine speed-up is 3.2–4.7×. The 15.2 s figure came from an earlier, slower environment.

- 2026-10-14 · **S1-F7 verification follow-ups.**
  - **Image re-encoding and the scan hook move to S3-03** (sharp arrives with the media pipeline; adding sharp now would be a heavy dependency ahead of its task). Acceptance check "an uploaded JPEG is stored without EXIF" is open and belongs to S3-03; verification images stay attachment-only downloads for staff until then.
  - **Dedupe, not `Idempotency-Key`:** the task allowed either; `(agency_id, sha256)` among unsubmitted documents needs no client change and no key store.
  - **Sweeper bound:** at most 200 pages × 500 objects per prefix per run, always from the start of the prefix; past ~100k objects per prefix it needs a persisted cursor (revisit in S3-03 with the media bucket).
  - **Staff `users.status`:** `app_staff` cannot read `users`, so `withStaffCtx` does one extra short `app_auth` read per staff request (staff traffic is low). Nothing sets `DISABLED` yet; the check is ready for when something does.
